payload.description: Umbrella for closing the gap that a leaked cluster-stored deployer key can stand up operational routes and (today) drain existing routes. Sub-issues cover: moving ISM + warp-route ownership to the hardware wallet, gating the relayer with a curated route whitelist, and minimizing the deploy-time signer. See docs/architecture-decisions.md (deployer authorization) and docs/ops-decisions.md.
payload.title: Harden warp-route deploy authorization & deployer-key custody (SVM bridge)

payload.description:
The core deployer SKIPS the multisig-ISM ownership transfer on a stale assumption. deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh:298-306 says "core transfer-ownership does not exist in the CLI ... Skipping", but `hyperlane-sealevel-client multisig-ism-message-id transfer-ownership --program-id <ism> <new-owner>` DOES exist (verified at the pinned monorepo sha 16c056a, client main.rs:676).

Impact: the ISM access-control owner = deployer key today. multisig-ism-message-id `SetValidatorsAndThreshold` enforces only owner-signer (processor.rs:374-376), so a leaked key can swap in attacker validators and forge messages for EVERY route on that ISM -> drain all collateral. This is the most severe residual hole.

Fix: replace the multisig_ism_message_id "Skipping" branch with a real transfer-ownership to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY, mirroring the working mailbox transfer-ownership block (deploy.sh:289-295). validator_announce has no owner / nothing owner-gated (instruction.rs = Init,Announce only) -> drop its warning, nothing to transfer. No monorepo bump needed (command present at the pin).
payload.title: Transfer multisig-ISM ownership to the hardware wallet during core deploy

payload.description:
warp-deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh transfers only the route programs BPF upgrade authority (solana program set-upgrade-authority, deploy.sh:254-259). The Hyperlane app-level owner is never moved, and build_side (deploy.sh:62-75) sets no owner -> defaults to the deployer key.

Impact: that owner gates enroll_remote_routers / set_interchain_security_module / set_destination_gas / transfer_ownership on each route. A leaked key can re-point a routers or change an existing route ISM and drain that route collateral.

Fix: after deploy + the upgrade-authority transfer, call `hyperlane-sealevel-client token transfer-ownership` (exists at pin, main.rs:346; --token-type Native|Synthetic|Collateral per side, --program-id) to move each side owner to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY. Run LAST, after all owner-gated config (enroll/set-ISM/set-dest-gas) the client does during deploy. Note: once transferred, FORCE_REDEPLOY of an EXISTING route requires the hardware wallet (Ledger) to sign owner ops - acceptable/expected.
payload.title: Transfer warp-route app-level ownership to the hardware wallet during warp deploy

payload.description:
Relayer relays EVERY message between gorchain<->solana: no whitelist set, and HYP_GASPAYMENTENFORCEMENT=[{"type":"none"}] (docker-compose-hyperlane-relayer.yml). Empty MatchingList = relay-all (relayer matching_list.rs:369-375). The mailbox is permissionless (processor.rs dispatch/process), so any deployed route is operational with ZERO operator action; the warp-UI listing is cosmetic.

HYP_WHITELIST is a built-in relayer MatchingList setting (relayer settings mod.rs:50, loaded via the HYP_ env prefix, hyperlane-base loader mod.rs:98) -> config only, no agent code.

Fix: populate HYP_WHITELIST with blessed routes recipient addresses (recipientaddress = H256 hex from each route program-ids.json), assembled in the ops layer from the CURATED git route menu (mirror the warpRoutes.yaml build path), regenerated + relayer restarted when a route is added.

CRITICAL: derive from the curated git source, NOT on-chain discovery - else a leaked-key rogue route auto-whitelists itself and the gate is void. Updating the whitelist is an ops/git-reviewed config change (NOT Ledger): that is the route-endorsement governance gate.
payload.title: Gate the relayer with HYP_WHITELIST built from the curated route menu

payload.description: publish-bridge-state.yml regex-patches deployment-derived scalars (IGP IDs, mailbox, and now HYP_WHITELIST per hyp-d9c.3) into committed specs (spec-relayer.yml/spec-gas-oracle.yml/spec-warp-ui.yml) then commits+pushes. Preferred: derive these on-the-fly from the deployer's generated/ artifacts at deploy time instead of mutating committed specs. Separate concern from hyp-d9c; raised during the authz-hardening design 2026-06-09.
payload.title: Derive prod consumer config from generated artifacts (drop committed-spec patching)

payload.description:
The ops layer (PRs #25/#30) implemented bring-up (deploy-all.yml, setup-all.yml, prepare-chains, distribute-credentials, configure-dns, publish-bridge-state, stop-all) but NONE of the operator-attended maintenance playbooks the design calls for. docs/ops-decisions.md:54-62 specifies seven composite playbooks; ops/playbooks/ contains none of them:

  kill-switch.yml      MISSING
  restore.yml          MISSING
  ism-update.yml       MISSING
  teardown.yml         MISSING
  add-validator.yml    MISSING
  remove-validator.yml MISSING
  verify-ownership.yml MISSING

Trigger: ops can now deploy N validators off validators.yaml (deploy-all.yml Validators play, ~lines 132-186) — pod + MinIO IAM + DNS — but nothing updates the on-chain multisig ISM validator set. A newly-deployed validator announces to validator-announce and writes checkpoints to MinIO, but its H160 is not in any ISM, so the relayer's ISM verification ignores its signatures. The deployment side and the on-chain side were designed as separate operator actions (docs/architecture-decisions.md:310-312); only the deployment side shipped.

All on-chain steps sign via the forked hyperlane-sealevel-client with BUILT-IN LEDGER support (--keypair usb://ledger...), run on the operator's localhost, sign+broadcast in one step (docs/ops-decisions.md:7-45). 

BLOCKED ON: validation of the Ledger-support PRs (forked sealevel-client + hyperlane fork) currently under test. Implementation should not start until that signing path is confirmed working.

Reference: the archived single-validator k8s-Job pattern in deployment/ops-archive/scripts/restore.sh + templates/restore-job.yml.j2 shows the old set-validators-and-threshold call shape (pre-Ledger, pre-ansible). Authoritative spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-ops-layer-redesign-and-ledger-signing-design.md. Builds on the ISM-ownership-handoff work in hyp-d9c (Ledger owns the ISM, so it can authorize set-validators-and-threshold).
payload.title: Implement operator-attended bridge maintenance ops playbooks (Ledger-signed)

payload.description: see above
payload.title: ism-update.yml — set ISM (validators, threshold) per chain, Ledger-signed

payload.description: Structural gap behind hyp-81f: the deployer Job can only ever set ONE validator per chain on-chain. deployer-multisig-config/{gorchain,solana}-multisig.json.tmpl hardcode a single ${X_VALIDATOR_ADDRESS} scalar with threshold 1; the scalars come from group_vars/all.yml (ops/inventories/prod/group_vars/all.yml:58-59) and are rendered once by deploy.sh:190-218. There is no path for a multi-validator initial deployment. Decide whether the deployer should derive its multisig config from validators.yaml (same H160-resolution logic ism-update needs) so a fresh deploy and a later ism-update agree on the data source, or whether initial deploy stays single-validator and ism-update is the only multi-validator path. Coupled to hyp-81f's data-model decision.
payload.title: Make initial ISM config multi-validator (derive from validators.yaml)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/kill-switch.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:56). Emergency halt: 'deployment stop' the agents, then set ISM validators to the null set per chain via the Ledger client (set-validators-and-threshold with the 0x0..0 sentinel, see deployment/ops-archive/scripts/*.sh for the old shape). Pairs with restore.yml. Reuses the ism-update set-validators primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: kill-switch.yml — stop agents + null the ISM validator set per chain

payload.description: ops/playbooks/restore.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:57). Inverse of kill-switch: set ISM validators back to the real set per chain (derived from validators.yaml) via the Ledger client, then 'deployment start' the agents. Reuses the ism-update primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: restore.yml — restore real ISM validator set + start agents

payload.description: ops/playbooks/add-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:60). Interactive: generate spec-validator-<label>.yml + edit validators.yaml, human gate (commit/PR/merge), then distribute-credentials -> configure-dns -> minio resync -> deploy the validator via stack_deploy. On-chain ISM addition is a SEPARATE ism-update.yml run (hyp-81f) — this playbook only stands up the pod/MinIO-IAM/DNS. Mirrors the existing deploy-all.yml Validators play (lines ~132-186) but for a single new validator.
payload.title: add-validator.yml — deployment-side validator onboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/remove-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:61). Pre-flight: ism-update.yml (hyp-81f) must have detached the validator from the ISM first. Then: 'deployment stop' the validator -> interactive spec deletion + validators.yaml edit + commit gate -> MinIO IAM cleanup (delete the per-validator user, keep its bucket) -> remove DNS. Per-validator MinIO IAM model is in ops/roles/credentials (PR #18, 93bfba3).
payload.title: remove-validator.yml — deployment-side validator offboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/teardown.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:59). Operator-attended multi-step flow: 'deployment stop' agents -> loop {claim IGP fees per chain} -> loop {close program} -> close orphan buffers -> loop {transfer SOL per wallet} -> optional key disposal. Each on-chain step signs on the Ledger. Sequencing/pauses/retry belong in the playbook, not a shell script. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: teardown.yml — attended bridge teardown (fees, programs, SOL, keys)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/verify-ownership.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:62). Read-only, no signing: confirm every deployed program (mailbox, ISM, IGP, validator-announce, warp routes) is owned by the hardware-wallet address. Companion to the hyp-d9c ownership handoff. Note: hyp-405 (Extend verify-ownership to check app-level ISM/route owners) is the follow-up that broadens this once the base playbook exists — base implementation belongs here.
payload.title: verify-ownership.yml — read-only program-ownership audit

payload.body: Resolved by #34 (a7ad1a5): deployment-derived values (mailbox, IGP program-ids/accounts, relayer whitelist) now render at deploy time from generated/ via ops/roles/stack_deploy/tasks/render_spec.yml — committed specs hold placeholder tokens (__GORCHAIN_MAILBOX__, __*_IGP_*__, __RELAYER_WHITELIST__) substituted into the on-host spec, gated by spec_render_generated. publish-bridge-state.yml no longer patches specs; it commits only generated/.

DEFERRED (2026-06-10): maintenance ops (this epic, incl. ism-update 564.1 and add/remove-validator 564.5/.6) deferred. Priority order: (1) WebSocket-based indexing (must land before deployment — it changes how the bridge indexes chains), (2) bridge deployment, (3) this epic. ism-update design is captured at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-ism-update-playbook-design.md (design-only, no code). Resume at the writing-plans step.

payload.description: Replace poll-based event detection with WebSocket subscriptions, make Solana/gorchain commitment configurable, and remove every multi-second sleep from the message critical path. Target ~2.5-4s gorchain / ~3-5s solana delivery in fast (confirmed) mode. Must land BEFORE bridge deployment (changes how the bridge indexes chains). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-websocket-fast-bridging-design.md (supersedes the 2026-05-25 tentative spec; adversarially reviewed 2026-06-10 — old spec covered only 1 of 3 polling stages, omitted gorchain, and routed a secret into committed state).

Fix (spec §6): (1) placeholders in artifacts, agents get real URLs via HYP_CHAINS_<CHAIN>_CUSTOMRPCURLS/CUSTOMWSURLS env overrides from spec secrets (parser support verified: hyperlane-base settings/parser/mod.rs:189 parse_base_and_override_urls is generic); (2) publish gate task scans staged generated/ for secret values + api-key= pattern, fails play on hit. Independent of WS work; merges first.

payload.description: New chains/hyperlane-sealevel/src/pubsub.rs (~100-150 lines) on solana_pubsub_client (workspace dep solana-pubsub-client=3.0, unused today): subscribe at the SAME commitment as indexing_commitment, notify_waiters on event, 60s pings (Helius 10min idle drop), reconnect w/ backoff, silent fallback to timer. ConnectionConf gains ws_url; config via wsUrls/customWsUrls mirroring rpcUrls/customRpcUrls (parser/mod.rs:189) so HYP_CHAINS_<CHAIN>_CUSTOMWSURLS works. Expose via NEW Indexer<T> trait method wake_signal() default None (avoids ContractSync::new signature change + downcasting); ContractSync select!{sleep, notified} at mod.rs:265-273. CRITICAL (missed by old spec): validator has TWO loops — SealevelMerkleTreeHookIndexer (accountSubscribe on merkle tree account; covered by shared ContractSync change) and checkpoint_submitter (submit.rs:121-166, NOT a ContractSync — pass Notify in, select! at sleeps lines 152+165). Validator must be event-driven or relayer loses the checkpoint race into 5s/10s/30s backoff (pending_message.rs:922). Spec §4.2/§2.
payload.title: Fork: WebSocket wake-up for relayer AND validator (pubsub.rs + Indexer::wake_signal)

payload.description: Add indexing_commitment to ConnectionConf (trait_builder.rs:15-30), thread through hardcoded finalized reads: account.rs:39 (3 callers: mailbox_indexer.rs:82,179 + interchain_gas.rs:139), mailbox_indexer.rs:101,201, interchain_gas.rs:159, merkle_tree_hook.rs:68 (+relax assertion msgs :22,:36), rpc/client.rs:136,165,222,251. LEAVE finalized: provider.rs:176-180 blockhash fetch. Chain-level commitment key, env HYP_CHAINS_<CHAIN>_COMMITMENT. Security: the risky hop is the VALIDATOR signing over a confirmed slot — destination mint can't be clawed back on origin rollback; no safe hybrid (validator gates delivery). Default finalized; fast mode explicit opt-in. WS subscription commitment MUST match (else wasted wake-ups). Spec §4.1/D5.
payload.title: Fork: configurable commitment level (finalized default, confirmed opt-in)

payload.description: New env vars (chain-specific canonical pattern): SOLANA_WS_URL (SECRET — Helius key; spec secrets: like SOLANA_RPC_URL), GORCHAIN_WS_URL, SOLANA_COMMITMENT/GORCHAIN_COMMITMENT. Delivery env-only via HYP_CHAINS_*_CUSTOMRPCURLS/CUSTOMWSURLS/COMMITMENT in relayer+validator compose — agent-config.json/registry carry placeholders only (depends on hyp-f9d). Keep-in-sync ripple: compose -> deployment/spec-*.yml -> tests/e2e/fixtures/test-spec-*.yml -> stack_env_vars in ops/inventories/*/group_vars/all.yml. Gorchain WS reachability: pubsub on RPC port+1 (8900); e2e external-services ip: entries gain WS port (gorchain-rpc:8900, solana :18900); prod/staging expose 8900 + verify proxy passes wss upgrade. e2e: (1) WS happy path w/ subscription-establishment log assert, (2) kill-WS fallback to timer polling, (3) confirmed-mode smoke beating finalized baseline, (4) secret-free state asserts, (5) warp-ui mode-flag fixture check. Spec §5/§8.
payload.title: Stacks: WS/commitment env plumbing, gorchain WS port, e2e tests

payload.description: hyperlane-warp-ui-template fork. Fast mode inverts ordering: delivery (~3-5s) precedes origin finality (~13-15s); the gap IS the rollback window. Transfer view shows two independent signals: Delivered (existing delivery tracking) and Final (origin tx reached finalized — getSignatureStatuses upgrade-only check). Fast: Sent -> Delivered ('awaiting origin finality') -> Complete; never claim irreversibility before origin finality. Safe-mode collapse via runtime-injected flag (pod env at container start, like runtime route config — NOT build-time NEXT_PUBLIC inline), derived from the same SOLANA_COMMITMENT spec var the agents use, so UI and agents can't disagree; safe mode suppresses the finality badge (single-stage Sent -> Complete). Spec §7/D7.
payload.title: Warp-UI: dual-commitment UX (Delivered vs Final, safe-mode collapse)

payload.description: Rebase gorbagana branch (2 commits: 82ab03c064 CI removal, a2f6ef11b0 Ledger signing) onto upstream 4da9c4419a (agents v2.2.0 release). Upstream didn't touch rust/sealevel/client in range — Ledger commit rebases clean. Contract sources are semantically unchanged in range (only a variable-name typo fix in mailbox/src/processor.rs + build-script churn; verified 2026-06-10). Convert kms-endpoint.patch + s3-path-style.patch (container-build/gorbagana-dev-hyperlane-agent/) into commits, checking v2.2.0 didn't obsolete them (s3_storage.rs/signers.rs saw only chore+tron churn); drop patch steps from the Dockerfile. Retag (sealevel-vX.Y.Z-gorbagana.N), rebuild agent+deployer images. Nothing is deployed yet (staging included) — the new base is the first provenance pin for every environment. Spec §4.0/D1/D2.

wss://rpc.gorbagana.wtf/ upgrade handshake returns 502 (backpack.gorbagana.wtf too) while HTTP RPC on the same host is healthy (getHealth ok) — verified 2026-06-10. Node side is fine: agave runs --full-rpc-api with pubsub on 8900 bound 0.0.0.0; gorbagana-rpc compose exposes 8900; envoy-rpc.yaml routes Upgrade: websocket to agave_ws:8900. Root cause: gorbagana-rpc deployment/spec.yml declares websocket: true routes but SO's http-proxy has NO websocket support — key silently ignored (verified: zero handling in stack-orchestrator/stack_orchestrator/deploy/). Workaround patch-caddy-websocket.sh (gorbagana-rpc stacks/gorchain-rpc/deploy/) PUTs an in-memory route via Caddy admin API: lost on Caddy restart, dials a {deployment-id}-service FQDN that goes stale on redeploy, and forces ingress protocols to [h1] globally. Fix: native websocket: true support in SO ingress generation (deploy/k8s/cluster_info.py — SO is under our control), delete the patch script. Fallback: expose 8900 directly on the gorchain host. Gates prod/staging WS rollout for the bridge agents (they need gorchain WS whenever off the RPC host).
payload.title: Gorchain public WS endpoint broken (502) — SO http-proxy ignores websocket: true

payload.body: Design validated 2026-06-10: SO-only fix (no controller access needed) — SO generates a per-deployment ws-mux (caddy:2-alpine ConfigMap+Deployment+Service) doing the Upgrade split; Ingress gets a single backend per (host,path), fixing the duplicate-paths bug too. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-so-websocket-ingress-design.md. First implementation step is the §6 spike (101 handshake through controller→mux without the h1 forcing).

payload.description: Minor findings from final review of the SO websocket-mux implementation (stack-orchestrator branch websocket-mux), none blocking: (1) _path_matcher glob /sub* also matches /subother — diverges from Ingress Prefix segment semantics; fix with 'path /sub /sub/*' (ws_mux.py:_path_matcher). (2) host/path interpolated raw into the Caddyfile — operator-authored so not a security boundary, but reject whitespace/braces/quotes in validate_http_proxy_routes as defense-in-depth. (3) collect_mux_entries splits proxy-to with bare unpack — malformed extra-colon value raises ugly ValueError at up; align with plain-route tolerance or validate format at create. (4) removing all websocket routes from a spec leaves the old mux Deployment/Service/CM orphaned until down (harmless; Ingress no longer references it) — consider deleting mux objects at up when get_ws_mux_resources() is None. Context: hyp-d34.7, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-so-websocket-ingress-design.md.
payload.title: ws-mux follow-ups: path matcher semantics, input hardening, stale-mux GC

payload.body: SO implementation complete on stack-orchestrator branch websocket-mux (11 commits, 39 unit tests). Kind verification passed end-to-end: create-time validation rejects duplicate routes; single-backend ingress; 101 handshake + echo round-trip through controller→mux with NO h1 forcing (spec §6 risk did not materialize); controller-restart and stop/start-redeploy regressions green; down sweeps mux. Two extra fixes from final review: case-insensitive Upgrade matcher (header_regexp, lowercase clients verified 101) and Caddyfile-hash pod annotation (config changes roll the mux). Bonus fix: disable-ssl-redirect annotation on no-TLS (kind) ingresses — previously ALL kind HTTP routes 308d into cert-less HTTPS. Remaining: Task 9 rollout (SO merge + host upgrade + gorbagana-rpc patch-script removal + live wss check).

TLS round verified locally (2026-06-10, kind + self-signed SAN cert via Ingress spec.tls): HTTPS GET through controller→mux returns 200 over negotiated HTTP/2; wss handshake (ALPN http/1.1, the real WS-client path) → 101; encrypted websocat echo round-trip OK. ALPN concern closed — no protocol forcing needed. OPERATIONAL NOTE for rollout: fork controller has a cert-load ordering quirk — it pushes Caddy config BEFORE writing Ingress-TLS secret pems to /etc/caddy/certs (load_folders), and skips re-push when regenerated config is identical, so a newly-loaded cert isn't served until the next MATERIAL config push. Symptom: 'tlsv1 alert internal error' on a host whose secret exists. Workaround: apply+delete a dummy ingress (or any real ingress change) to force a push. Could explain transient TLS failures after fresh deploys on prod; ACME-issued certs go through caddy storage, not load_folders, so steady-state prod is unaffected.

RESOLVED — verified live on woodburn 2026-06-10 after SO upgrade + RPC redeploy: wss://rpc.gorbagana.wtf and wss://backpack.gorbagana.wtf handshake 101 (was 502); slotSubscribe returns subscription id and streams slotNotifications through LE TLS -> caddy ingress -> ws-mux -> agave:8900; getHealth ok on both hosts; http->https 308 redirect preserved (acme-email gate); agave pod untouched by the rollout (22d uptime, 0 restarts). patch-caddy-websocket.sh removed in gorbagana-rpc (branch drop-caddy-ws-patch, pending user push). Gorchain WS endpoint dependency for the fast-bridging epic (hyp-d34) is now UNBLOCKED.
